subject: Runtime safeguard exclusion request — impact assessment and temporary SLA amendment
messages:
From: Tom Walsh <tom.walsh@vantagehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: VantageHealth Security Team <security@vantagehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary SLA exclusion for content-filter/tool-call failures on launch

Hi Naomi —

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. As we prep for our May 4th go-live, our security team flagged a risk with automated content filtering and downstream tool-calls that may cause intermittent structured-output failures in sensitive clinical prompts. In particular:

- When the content filter triggers a synchronous tool-call (external verification), the additional round-trip can push token latency beyond our 300ms per-token target for some endpoints.
- In ~0.8% of requests during simulated peak load, structured output (JSON schema) returned partial/empty payloads when a filter bypass + tool re-run occurred.

We'd like to request a limited SLA exclusion that acknowledges these specific filter/tool-call failure modes for the first 90 days post-launch while our joint engineering teams iterate mitigations.

Can Redwood provide:
1) A short impact assessment (latency/backoff behavior)
2) A proposed carve-out text we can include in our SOW (specific to content-filter + tool-call induced failures)
3) Any temporary mitigations you can commit to (e.g., priority routing, extended retry windows, proactive alerts)

We're happy to share the diagnostics we ran — attaching the traces and the summary.

Thanks,
Tom Walsh
Director, Product Operations
VantageHealth

Attachments: vantage-filter-diagnostics-20270421.pdf

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Walsh <tom.walsh@vantagehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA exclusion for content-filter/tool-call failures on launch

Tom —

Received, thanks for the detailed diagnostics. I've looped in Ben (sales) and Marissa (runtime lead) so we can align quickly. Initial notes:

- We can scope a limited, time-boxed SLA amendment that explicitly enumerates "filter-triggered synchronous tool-call" and "structured-output partial responses" as exceptions to the standard uptime/latency SLO for the first 90 days.
- We need agreement on metrics (what percent of requests qualify), mitigation commitments, and an obs/alerting plan before we sign anything.

Action items for us:
- Redwood to provide an impact assessment and proposed legal-friendly carve-out language (Ben will draft).
- Runtime engineering to propose mitigations and monitoring thresholds (Marissa).
- Shared JIRA to track fixes and rollback conditions (I'll create SUP-5832).

Can you confirm the exact endpoints and load profile you used in the attached diagnostics? That will help calibrate the assessment.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Thu, Apr 22, 2027 at 09:03 AM Tom Walsh <tom.walsh@vantagehealth.com> wrote:
> (original message and attachments)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: temporary SLA amendment language for filter/tool-call exceptions

Hi Naomi/Marissa —

I've put together proposed wording for a 90-day time-boxed amendment we can send to VantageHealth for review. High-level:

- Scope: Exceptions apply only when (a) Redwood's content-safeguard filter triggers a synchronous external tool-call or verification that materially increases client-perceived token latency, or (b) when the filter+tool-call flow results in an incomplete or malformed structured output as defined by the customer's provided JSON schema.
- Threshold: Exception only triggers when the combined event rate for the customer's account is <= 1% of total requests in a given calendar day.
- Duration: 90 days from go-live, with a 30-day review checkpoint.
- Mitigations: Redwood commits to priority routing for impacted requests, enhanced retries (configurable up to 2 additional attempts with exponential backoff), and a dedicated weekly sync between engineering teams.

I've attached a doc with the proposed legal text (proposed-sla-exclusion-draft-Naomi-v1.docx). This is intentionally concise to keep procurement/legal cycles short. If Marissa can confirm the mitigation commitments and expected telemetry, I can push this to Tom and their procurement.

Ben
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: temporary SLA amendment language for filter/tool-call exceptions

Thanks — reviewed the diagnostics and Ben's draft. Technical stance and recommended conditions:

- Approve time-boxed exclusion in principle with the following must-haves:
  * Redwood attaches a mitigation runbook to the amendment (we'll provide an excerpt; see attached mitigation-runbook-snapshot.xlsx).
  * Telemetry: Redwood will produce a daily compliance report for the 90-day period showing event-rate, P95 token-latency for impacted endpoints, and a list of affected request IDs.
  * Threshold tweak: change the threshold to <= 1.0% peak-hour event rate (stricter than daily average).
  * Auto-rollback: if the event rate surpasses 2.5% for any rolling 7-day window, the exclusion is automatically revoked until remediation is in place.

- Operational commitments we can make now: priority routing for customer bursts, increase per-request retry attempts to 2 with jitter, and a daily alert to both teams when event-rate > 0.5% for the hour.

I'll mark SUP-5832 with the acceptance criteria and owners. We should also schedule a legal review early next week.

—Marissa
Director, Runtime Services
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Walsh <tom.walsh@vantagehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, VantageHealth Security Team <security@vantagehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Apr 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Final: temporary runtime safeguard exclusion — approval and next steps

Tom —

Thanks for patience while we reviewed this with engineering and runtime. Summary and next steps:

1) Decision: Redwood approves a 90-day, time-boxed SLA amendment covering the narrow failure modes you described ("filter-triggered synchronous tool-calls" and "filter-induced partial structured outputs"), subject to the conditions below.

2) Conditions (as agreed):
- Scope and timeframe: 90 days from your go-live date (May 4, 2027), with a checkpoint at day 30.
- Thresholds: exclusion applies only when the customer's peak-hour event rate <= 1.0% (with auto-rollback if 7-day rolling rate > 2.5%).
- Observability: Redwood will provide a daily dashboard and weekly compliance PDF with request IDs and P95 latency for impacted endpoints.
- Mitigations: priority routing, two retry attempts with exponential backoff/jitter, and on-call escalation during the 90-day period.
- Remediation plan: SUP-5832 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-5832) will track fixes; we will agree on completion criteria there.

3) Next steps:
- Ben will send the legal-friendly amendment text for your procurement team to sign. (Ben: please route to HubSpot deal RDW-4721.)
- I'll attach the mitigation runbook excerpt and the initial compliance report template.
- If VantageHealth agrees, we'll push the amendment into DocuSign by EOD Monday.

If that all reads OK, Ben — please send the one-page amendment and a DocuSign link. Tom — please confirm you accept the conditions so we can proceed.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: proposed-sla-exclusion-draft-Naomi-v1.docx, mitigation-runbook-snapshot.xlsx
